name: The blessed life of the righteous, contrasted with the wicked
place: the opening psalm, serving as a preface to the whole Book of Psalms
summary: The psalm contrasts the blessed life of the person who delights in God's law with the fate of the wicked — the righteous flourish like a fruitful tree, while the wicked are blown away like chaff.

name: Humanity crowned with glory and honor over creation
shortName: How majestic is your name in all the earth
place: echoes Genesis 1's account of humanity's dominion over creation
summary: David marvels that God gave humanity dominion and honor over the rest of the created world.

name: The heavens declaring God's glory and the perfection of his law
shortName: The heavens declare the glory of God
place: praised by C.S. Lewis as the greatest poem in the Psalter
summary: David moves from the silent testimony of the skies to praise for the perfect, trustworthy law of the Lord.

name: David's cry of abandonment turning to praise among the nations
shortName: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?
place: later quoted by Jesus during the crucifixion
summary: David cries out feeling forsaken by God while enemies close in, then turns from anguish to confident praise, anticipating that all the families of the nations will worship God.

name: The Lord as shepherd through green pastures and the darkest valley
place: the most widely known and memorized psalm, often read at funerals
summary: David pictures the Lord as a shepherd who provides rest, guidance, and protection even through the darkest valley, and as a generous host whose goodness follows him all his life.

name: The King of glory entering his gates
shortName: Who is this King of glory?
summary: David calls for the gates to lift up so the King of glory can enter in triumphant procession.

name: The relief of confessed and forgiven sin
shortName: Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven
place: quoted by Paul in Romans 4 as evidence that God counts righteousness apart from works
summary: David contrasts the misery of hiding his sin with the relief that came once he confessed it to God.

name: God as refuge amid earth's upheaval
shortName: God is our refuge and strength
place: the inspiration for Martin Luther's hymn "A Mighty Fortress Is Our God"
summary: The sons of Korah declare God a secure refuge even if the earth gives way and the mountains fall into the sea.

name: David's confession of his sin with Bathsheba and prayer for a clean heart
shortName: Create in me a clean heart
place: written after Nathan confronted David over Bathsheba
summary: David confesses his sin and pleads for God's mercy after Nathan the prophet confronted him, asking God to create a clean heart in him and restore his joy.

name: God's eternity and Moses' prayer to number our days
shortName: Teach us to number our days
place: the only psalm whose heading attributes it to Moses
summary: Moses contrasts God's everlasting existence with the brief, trouble-filled span of a human life, and prays that God would teach his people to number their days wisely.

name: The safety of dwelling in God's shelter
shortName: He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High
place: misquoted by Satan when tempting Jesus in the wilderness
summary: The psalmist describes the safety of the one who dwells in the shelter of the Most High, covered from danger.

name: A call to enter God's gates with thanksgiving
place: the basis of the hymn "All People That on Earth Do Dwell", sung to the Old Hundredth tune
summary: The psalmist calls all the earth to worship the Lord with joyful songs and thanksgiving.

name: David's roll call of God's benefits
shortName: Bless the Lord, O my soul
place: known for its imagery of sin removed "as far as the east is from the west"
summary: David calls himself to remember God's forgiveness, healing, and steady love toward him.

name: The Lord's unsleeping watch over his people
shortName: I lift up my eyes to the hills
place: part of the Psalms of Ascent, sung by pilgrims traveling to Jerusalem
summary: The psalmist answers his own question about where help comes from with the Lord, who watches over his people without slumbering.

name: A cry for mercy from the depths
shortName: Out of the depths I cry to you, O Lord
place: known in Latin as "De Profundis", one of the church's seven penitential psalms
summary: The psalmist cries out to God from deep distress over sin and waits for him the way a watchman waits for morning.

name: God's intimate knowledge of David's heart and mind
shortName: You have searched me and known me
summary: David reflects on how thoroughly God knows his thoughts, words, and actions, and invites God to search his heart and lead him in the way everlasting.

name: David's praise of God's greatness across generations
shortName: Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised
place: an acrostic psalm that works through the Hebrew alphabet in order
summary: David praises God's greatness and goodness, celebrating that the Lord is gracious and near to all who call on him.

name: A call for everything that breathes to praise God with every instrument
shortName: Let everything that has breath praise the Lord
place: the closing doxology of the entire Book of Psalms
summary: The psalmist lists instruments from trumpet to cymbals as fitting ways to praise God, and the whole Psalter closes with a call for everything that has breath to praise the Lord.
